title: Queues & Deques
subtitle: A queue preserves arrival order; a deque also keeps only the live candidates needed at either boundary.
variables: n = input items, k = window size or capacity, V/E = all supplied graph vertices/edges (including neighbor-only vertices and edges scanned during validation), R/C = grid rows/columns, w = maximum BFS frontier width (or retained event count in RecentCounter), q = current queue size. Bounds assume O(1) reference operations and fixed-size numeric comparisons/arithmetic; Python large integers cost by bit length. Hash-based graph bounds are expected and include O(key length) hashing/comparison for long keys. Auxiliary space excludes returned output unless stated; deque storage itself is counted. Inputs are finite; graphs use hashable vertices. Single-threaded algorithms are not producer/consumer synchronization. For lock-state templates d = wheel count; O(d) string neighbor construction and hashing is charged per generated neighbor.

decisionProcess: 0–30s: define the queued record (vertex, cell, candidate index, timestamp or cyclic turn), output, and whether arrivals/edges are ordered.
30–60s: equal-cost shortest moves -> BFS; nearest of many sources -> seed all; weights0/1 -> relax with deque; other nonnegative weights -> heap Dijkstra. Negative weights require another algorithm.
60–90s: fixed-window extremum -> monotonic deque; max-min validity -> dual deques; shortest sum with negatives -> increasing prefix deque. Prove both dominance and expiry.
90–120s: dependencies -> Kahn indegree; two groups -> component coloring; repeated turns -> simulate only after bounding total turns.

120–180s: for API design choose eviction/rejection/blocking, then deque/ring/two stacks. State invariant, amortized versus worst latency, memory including payloads/output, and dry-run empty, duplicate and boundary cases.

templateDetails.preconditions: Numeric sequence may contain negatives; target may be nonpositive. Returns shortest NONEMPTY contiguous length or -1; no mutation. Feasibility loop precedes dominance removal.
templateDetails.observation: Feasibility removal precedes dominance, preserving nonempty cases.

templateDetails.preconditions: Directed mapping to reusable lists of (hashable neighbor, 0/1 weight); validates all supplied edges. Returns reachable vertex distances only; source absent is allowed. No mutation; undirected graphs need symmetric edges.
templateDetails.observation: Zero front/one back maintain distance bands; stale records are not current.

templateDetails.preconditions: n labeled vertices 0..n-1; directed edge (u,v) means u precedes v. Returns one order, or [] for a cycle (also [] for n=0). Parallel edges are counted separately; no mutation.
templateDetails.observation: Zero indegree means all prerequisites already removed.

templateDetails.preconditions: Positive integer capacity; enqueue returns success bool and never evicts. peek/dequeue raise IndexError when empty; None is a valid item. No resizing; no thread-safety guarantee.
templateDetails.observation: Size distinguishes full from empty at identical modular head/tail.

templateDetails.preconditions: FIFO object; arbitrary payloads. Empty pop/peek raise IndexError. Internal transfer mutates representation but not payloads.
templateDetails.observation: Transfer reverses each item only once.

templateDetails.preconditions: Finite numeric nondecreasing timestamps, duplicates counted individually. Returns count in inclusive [t-window,t]. Rejected out-of-order ping leaves state unchanged.
templateDetails.observation: Inclusive cutoff expires only strictly older timestamps.

templateDetails.preconditions: Undirected adjacency list with vertices 0..n-1 and symmetric edges; reusable lists. Returns bool; empty graph is bipartite, self-loop is not. Does not mutate; symmetry is a caller precondition.
templateDetails.observation: An odd cycle forces a same-color edge.

templateDetails.preconditions: Nonempty R/D string with optimal bans against the earliest upcoming opponent. Returns winning party; no mutation. Re-enqueued index is next-cycle turn. Arbitrary round-robin simulations need their own turn bound.
templateDetails.observation: Each contest permanently eliminates one participant.

templateDetails.preconditions: d-wheel decimal lock, unit moves change one digit with wraparound. Minimum moves or -1; consumes deadends iterable, no input mutation. d=4 has 10,000 states. Each of O(d) neighbors costs O(d) string copying/hashing; general dimension bound is not O(10^d d). D is supplied deadend count; deadend set construction/validation adds O(D*d) time and stored key characters, even if start is forbidden.
templateDetails.observation: A state must encode every future-relevant fact.

templateDetails.preconditions: Positive integer capacity. Appends reject full writes with False, pops raise IndexError on empty. None is valid data. Mutates own fixed buffer and releases removed references; no thread-safety.
templateDetails.observation: Front insertion moves head before storing; tail deletion leaves head unchanged.

practiceDetails.insight: Expire timestamps strictly before inclusive cutoff.
Reverse incoming only when outgoing empty.
Prepend moves head left before writing; pop uses head+size-1.
Take last node of each left-to-right level.
All rotten sources start at minute0; count unreachable fresh cells.
Seed all zero cells, not one BFS per cell.
Eight directions and blocked endpoints; cell-count length differs from edge count.
Visited state is complete wheel string; dead start fails.
Processed count less than V proves directed cycle.
Remove ready prerequisites and preserve all isolated vertices.
Restart coloring in every disconnected component.
Surviving senator next acts at old index+n.
Max and min together certify range validity.
New lower prefix dominates older higher prefix, while feasible fronts minimize length.
Follow outgoing arrow at cost0, other directions cost1.
